|Abstract||Background: People with intellectual disabilities (ID) often present with challenging behaviour. The impact of challenging behaviour on carers and on the quality of life of the person with ID is significant. This paper reports on the development and testing of a brief intervention for challenging behaviour in people with ID. Method: A randomized controlled trial with a brief intervention (3 sessions) for challenging behaviour was undertaken. Participants were adults with ID who presented with challenging behaviour. Primary outcome measures were challenging behaviour, quality of life, and carer burden. Secondary outcome measures were the participant's mental health and carer's mental health. Results: The brief intervention was effective in reducing challenging behaviour and increasing quality of life and carer burden. The intervention was also effective in reducing carer mental health problems. Conclusion: The results indicate that the brief intervention was effective in reducing challenging behaviour and increasing quality of life. The results are discussed in relation to the possible mechanisms of change, including the effects of the intervention on the carers and on the social environment of the participant.|
